For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=0,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=0-(-\frac{1}{2})=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y(2{x}^{3}+3)+{y}_{\text{new}}(2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}+3))\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}y(2{x}^{3}+3)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{4}y(2{x}^{3}+3)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}+3) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}y(2{x}^{3}+7)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}+3) & =\frac{1}{4}y(2{x}^{3}+7) \\ \frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(1-2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}) & =\frac{1}{4}y(2{x}^{3}+7) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y(2{x}^{3}+7)}{1-2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=0.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y(2{x}^{3}+7)}{1-2({x}_{\text{new}})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{3}(2\cdot {(-\frac{1}{2})}^{3}+7)}{1-2\cdot {0}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{9}{4} \\  & ≈2.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y(0)≈2.25.$

For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c, the trapezoidal method with step size Δx is given by Δy=12(y′+ynew′)⋅Δx, with ynew′=f(xnew,ynew) evaluated at the next x and y values.

First, since we want to find the value of y at x=0, we will use a step size of

Δx=0−(−12)=12.

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, Δy is given by

Δy=12(y′+ynew′)⋅Δx=12(y(2x3+3)+ynew(2(xnew)3+3))⋅12=14y(2x3+3)+14ynew(2(xnew)3+3).

We substitute this into ynew=y+Δy:

ynew=y+Δyynew=y+14y(2x3+3)+14ynew(2(xnew)3+3)ynew=14y(2x3+7)+14ynew(2(xnew)3+3).

Then, we solve for the general formula for ynew:

ynew−14ynew(2(xnew)3+3)=14y(2x3+7)14ynew(1−2(xnew)3)=14y(2x3+7)ynew=y(2x3+7)1−2(xnew)3

Now, in the first step, the new x value is xnew=−12+12=0. Hence, the new y value is

ynew=y(2x3+7)1−2(xnew)3=13(2⋅(−12)3+7)1−2⋅03=94≈2.25.

Therefore, we conclude that y(0)≈2.25.
